## File: backend/app/db.py
```python
"""SQLite access: connections, the ``get_db`` dependency and schema migrations.

The application uses the standard library's :mod:`sqlite3` directly. There is
no ORM: queries are short and explicit, and every value goes through a ``?``
placeholder so that user input can never change the meaning of a statement.

Connections
-----------
Endpoints never open connections. They declare a dependency::

    @router.get("/things")
    def list_things(conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)):
        rows = conn.execute("SELECT id, name FROM things").fetchall()

``get_db`` hands out a connection whose rows are :class:`sqlite3.Row` objects
(columns readable by name, ``row["name"]``) and with foreign keys enforced. The
work done during one request is committed when the endpoint returns normally
and rolled back if it raises.

Migrations
----------
The schema is defined by :data:`MIGRATIONS`, a list of SQL scripts applied in
order. The number of scripts already applied is stored in SQLite's
``user_version`` pragma, so :func:`init_db` only runs the new ones. To change
the schema, **append** a script; never edit or reorder the existing entries,
because databases in use have already run them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import threading
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import datetime, timezone

#: Schema scripts, applied in order. Append only.
MIGRATIONS: list[str] = [
    # 1: users. ``username`` is unique without regard to case, so "Alice" and
    # "alice" cannot both register.
    """
    CREATE TABLE users (
        id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        username      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
        password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,
        created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL
    );
    """,
    # 2: an audit trail of security-relevant events (sign-ins, failed sign-ins).
    """
    CREATE TABLE audit_log (
        id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        user_id    INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
        event      TEXT    NOT NULL,
        detail     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
        created_at TEXT    NOT NULL
    );
    CREATE INDEX audit_log_user ON audit_log(user_id, created_at);
    """,
    # 3: personal todos. Each row belongs to exactly one user; deleting the
    # user removes their todos. ``done`` is stored as 0/1 because SQLite has no
    # boolean type.
    """
    CREATE TABLE todos (
        id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        title      TEXT    NOT NULL,
        done       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        created_at TEXT    NOT NULL,
        updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL
    );
    CREATE INDEX todos_user ON todos(user_id, created_at);
    """,
]


def utc_now() -> str:
    """The current time in UTC as an ISO 8601 string, e.g. ``2026-11-24T12:00:00+00:00``.

    All timestamps are stored in this form. Strings in this format sort in the
    same order as the times they represent, so ``ORDER BY created_at`` works.
    """
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def connect(path: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open a connection configured the way the application expects.

    * rows are :class:`sqlite3.Row`, so columns can be read by name;
    * foreign key constraints are enforced (SQLite leaves them off by default);
    * ``check_same_thread`` is off because FastAPI may run a request's
      dependencies and endpoint in different worker threads. Each connection is
      still used by one request at a time.
    """
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn


def schema_version(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
    """How many entries of :data:`MIGRATIONS` have been applied to this database."""
    return int(conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0])


def init_db(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
    """Apply the migrations this database has not run yet; return how many ran.

    Each script runs in its own transaction together with the update of
    ``user_version``, so a failing script leaves the database at the previous
    version instead of half migrated.
    """
    applied = 0
    for number, script in enumerate(MIGRATIONS, start=1):
        if number <= schema_version(conn):
            continue
        with conn:
            conn.executescript(f"BEGIN;\n{script}\nPRAGMA user_version = {number};\nCOMMIT;")
        applied += 1
    return applied


class Database:
    """Owns the database of one application instance.

    For a file database every request gets its own connection. An in-memory
    database (``":memory:"``) exists only as long as its connection, so in that
    case a single shared connection is kept for the life of the application and
    access to it is serialised with a lock.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self._shared: sqlite3.Connection | None = None
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        if path == ":memory:":
            self._shared = connect(path)
            init_db(self._shared)
        else:
            with connect(path) as conn:
                init_db(conn)

    def connections(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        """Yield one connection for a request, committing or rolling back afterwards."""
        if self._shared is not None:
            with self._lock:
                try:
                    yield self._shared
                    self._shared.commit()
                except BaseException:
                    self._shared.rollback()
                    raise
            return
        conn = connect(self.path)
        try:
            yield conn
            conn.commit()
        except BaseException:
            conn.rollback()
            raise
        finally:
            conn.close()


_database: Database | None = None


def configure(database: Database) -> None:
    """Make ``database`` the one :func:`get_db` hands connections from."""
    global _database
    _database = database


def get_db() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    """FastAPI dependency: a connection for the current request.

    Usage::

        def endpoint(conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db)): ...

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: if the application was not created through
            :func:`app.main.create_app`, which configures the database.
    """
    if _database is None:
        raise RuntimeError("database not configured: create the app with create_app()")
    yield from _database.connections()


def audit(conn: sqlite3.Connection, event: str, user_id: int | None = None, detail: str = "") -> None:
    """Record a security-relevant event in ``audit_log``.

    Use short event names such as ``"login"``, ``"login_failed"`` or
    ``"register"``. ``detail`` is free text for humans; never put passwords or
    tokens in it.
    """
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO audit_log (user_id, event, detail, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (user_id, event, detail, utc_now()),
    )


def row_to_dict(row: sqlite3.Row | None) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Turn a row into a plain dict (or keep ``None``), e.g. to return it as JSON."""
    return None if row is None else {key: row[key] for key in row.keys()}
```

## File: backend/app/routers/auth.py
```python
"""Registration, sign-in and the current user.

Endpoints:

* ``POST /api/auth/register`` - create an account;
* ``POST /api/auth/login``    - exchange credentials for an access token;
* ``GET  /api/auth/me``       - the signed-in user.

Usernames are unique without regard to case (the column is ``COLLATE NOCASE``),
so "Alice" and "alice" are the same account. Sign-in answers the same 401 for an
unknown user and a wrong password, so the response does not reveal which
usernames exist.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sqlite3

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.db import audit, get_db, utc_now
from app.errors import bad_request, conflict, unauthorized
from app.security import (
    CurrentUser,
    create_access_token,
    get_current_user,
    hash_password,
    password_problem,
    verify_password,
)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])

#: Usernames are 3-32 characters of letters, digits, ``_`` or ``-``.
USERNAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$")


class RegisterRequest(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``POST /api/auth/register``."""

    username: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)
    password: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1024)


class UserOut(BaseModel):
    """A user as returned by the API. Never includes the password hash."""

    id: int
    username: str
    created_at: str


class LoginRequest(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``POST /api/auth/login``."""

    username: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)
    password: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1024)


class TokenOut(BaseModel):
    """What a successful sign-in returns."""

    access_token: str
    token_type: str = "bearer"
    expires_in: int


@router.post(
    "/register",
    response_model=UserOut,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Create an account.",
)
def register(
    body: RegisterRequest,
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> UserOut:
    """Create a user and return it.

    Raises:
        ApiError: 400 ``invalid_username`` for a malformed name, 400
            ``weak_password`` for a password that is too short, 409
            ``username_taken`` when the name is already in use.
    """
    username = body.username.strip()
    if not USERNAME_PATTERN.match(username):
        raise bad_request(
            "invalid_username",
            "Username must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits, '_' or '-'.",
        )
    problem = password_problem(body.password)
    if problem is not None:
        raise bad_request("weak_password", problem)

    existing = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ?", (username,)
    ).fetchone()
    if existing is not None:
        raise conflict("username_taken", "That username is already taken.")

    created_at = utc_now()
    try:
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO users (username, password_hash, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (username, hash_password(body.password), created_at),
        )
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
        # A concurrent registration won the race between the check and insert.
        raise conflict("username_taken", "That username is already taken.") from exc

    user_id = int(cursor.lastrowid)
    audit(conn, "register", user_id=user_id)
    return UserOut(id=user_id, username=username, created_at=created_at)


@router.post("/login", response_model=TokenOut, summary="Sign in and get a token.")
def login(
    body: LoginRequest,
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
    settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings),
) -> TokenOut:
    """Check credentials and return an access token.

    Raises:
        ApiError: 401 ``invalid_credentials`` for an unknown user or a wrong
            password (the same answer for both).
    """
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, username, password_hash FROM users WHERE username = ?",
        (body.username.strip(),),
    ).fetchone()

    if row is None or not verify_password(body.password, row["password_hash"]):
        audit(conn, "login_failed", user_id=None if row is None else row["id"])
        raise unauthorized("invalid_credentials", "Wrong username or password.")

    audit(conn, "login", user_id=row["id"])
    token = create_access_token(row["id"], row["username"], settings)
    return TokenOut(access_token=token, token_type="bearer", expires_in=settings.token_ttl)


@router.get("/me", response_model=UserOut, summary="The signed-in user.")
def me(
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> UserOut:
    """Return the account the request's token belongs to."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, username, created_at FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user.id,)
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:  # pragma: no cover - get_current_user already checked
        raise unauthorized("invalid_token", "Your session is invalid or has expired.")
    return UserOut(id=row["id"], username=row["username"], created_at=row["created_at"])
```

## File: backend/app/routers/todos.py
```python
"""Personal todo lists.

Every endpoint works only on the signed-in user's todos. A todo that belongs to
someone else is reported as 404 ``todo_not_found``, exactly like a missing one,
so a client cannot probe which identifiers exist.

A todo in JSON is ``{"id", "title", "done", "created_at", "updated_at"}``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query, Response, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.db import get_db, utc_now
from app.errors import bad_request, not_found
from app.pagination import PageParams, page_params, paginate
from app.security import CurrentUser, get_current_user

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/todos", tags=["todos"])

TITLE_MAX = 200


class TodoOut(BaseModel):
    """A todo as returned by the API."""

    id: int
    title: str
    done: bool
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str


class TodoCreate(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``POST /api/todos``."""

    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=TITLE_MAX)


class TodoUpdate(BaseModel):
    """Body of ``PATCH /api/todos/{id}``; omitted fields are left unchanged."""

    title: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=TITLE_MAX)
    done: bool | None = None


def _to_out(row: sqlite3.Row) -> TodoOut:
    return TodoOut(
        id=row["id"],
        title=row["title"],
        done=bool(row["done"]),
        created_at=row["created_at"],
        updated_at=row["updated_at"],
    )


def _load(conn: sqlite3.Connection, user_id: int, todo_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row:
    """Fetch one of the user's todos or raise 404 ``todo_not_found``."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, title, done, created_at, updated_at FROM todos WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?",
        (todo_id, user_id),
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise not_found("todo_not_found", f"Todo {todo_id} does not exist.")
    return row


@router.get("", summary="List the signed-in user's todos, newest first.")
def list_todos(
    done: bool | None = Query(default=None, description="Filter by completion."),
    page: PageParams = Depends(page_params),
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return one page of todos. ``?done=true|false`` narrows the list."""
    where = "user_id = ?"
    params: list[object] = [user.id]
    if done is not None:
        where += " AND done = ?"
        params.append(1 if done else 0)

    total = int(
        conn.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM todos WHERE {where}", params).fetchone()[0]
    )
    rows = conn.execute(
        f"SELECT id, title, done, created_at, updated_at FROM todos WHERE {where} "
        "ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
        (*params, page.limit, page.offset),
    ).fetchall()
    return paginate([_to_out(row) for row in rows], total, page)


@router.post(
    "",
    response_model=TodoOut,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Add a todo.",
)
def create_todo(
    body: TodoCreate,
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> TodoOut:
    """Create a todo for the signed-in user.

    Raises:
        ApiError: 400 ``invalid_title`` when the title is empty after trimming.
    """
    title = body.title.strip()
    if not title:
        raise bad_request("invalid_title", "Title must not be empty.")
    if len(title) > TITLE_MAX:
        raise bad_request("invalid_title", f"Title may be at most {TITLE_MAX} characters.")

    now = utc_now()
    cursor = conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO todos (user_id, title, done, created_at, updated_at) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, 0, ?, ?)",
        (user.id, title, now, now),
    )
    row = _load(conn, user.id, int(cursor.lastrowid))
    return _to_out(row)


@router.get("/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoOut, summary="One todo.")
def get_todo(
    todo_id: int,
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> TodoOut:
    """Return one of the signed-in user's todos."""
    return _to_out(_load(conn, user.id, todo_id))


@router.patch("/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoOut, summary="Change a todo's title or state.")
def update_todo(
    todo_id: int,
    body: TodoUpdate,
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> TodoOut:
    """Update the fields that are present in the body.

    Raises:
        ApiError: 400 ``invalid_title`` for an empty title, 404
            ``todo_not_found`` for a missing or foreign todo.
    """
    _load(conn, user.id, todo_id)

    changes: list[str] = []
    params: list[object] = []
    if body.title is not None:
        title = body.title.strip()
        if not title:
            raise bad_request("invalid_title", "Title must not be empty.")
        if len(title) > TITLE_MAX:
            raise bad_request("invalid_title", f"Title may be at most {TITLE_MAX} characters.")
        changes.append("title = ?")
        params.append(title)
    if body.done is not None:
        changes.append("done = ?")
        params.append(1 if body.done else 0)

    if changes:
        changes.append("updated_at = ?")
        params.append(utc_now())
        params.extend([todo_id, user.id])
        conn.execute(
            f"UPDATE todos SET {', '.join(changes)} WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?",
            params,
        )
    return _to_out(_load(conn, user.id, todo_id))


@router.delete(
    "/{todo_id}",
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
    summary="Delete a todo.",
)
def delete_todo(
    todo_id: int,
    user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_db),
) -> Response:
    """Delete one of the signed-in user's todos."""
    _load(conn, user.id, todo_id)
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM todos WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?", (todo_id, user.id))
    return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
```

## File: backend/app/main.py
```python
"""The application factory.

``uvicorn --factory app.main:build`` serves an application built from
environment settings. Tests and scripts call :func:`create_app` with explicit
values instead::

    app = create_app(db_path=":memory:", secret="test")

Adding a feature means writing a router module in :mod:`app.routers` and adding
one ``app.include_router(...)`` line below.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from app import __version__, errors
from app.config import Settings, get_settings, settings_from_env
from app.db import Database, configure
from app.routers import auth, health, todos

FRONTEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "frontend"


def create_app(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    *,
    db_path: str | None = None,
    secret: str | None = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Build a configured application.

    Args:
        settings: Complete settings. Read from the environment when omitted.
        db_path: Shortcut that overrides ``settings.db_path`` (tests use
            ``":memory:"``).
        secret: Shortcut that overrides ``settings.secret``.

    The database is opened and migrated here, so the application is ready to
    serve requests as soon as this returns.
    """
    if settings is None:
        settings = Settings(secret=secret or "") if secret is not None else settings_from_env()
    if db_path is not None or secret is not None:
        settings = Settings(
            db_path=db_path or settings.db_path,
            secret=secret or settings.secret,
            token_ttl=settings.token_ttl,
            cors_origins=settings.cors_origins,
            page_size=settings.page_size,
            max_page_size=settings.max_page_size,
        )
    settings.validate()

    app = FastAPI(title="Taskboard", version=__version__)
    app.dependency_overrides[get_settings] = lambda: settings
    configure(Database(settings.db_path))
    errors.install(app)

    if settings.cors_origins:
        app.add_middleware(
            CORSMiddleware,
            allow_origins=list(settings.cors_origins),
            allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"],
            allow_headers=["Authorization", "Content-Type"],
        )

    app.include_router(health.router)
    app.include_router(auth.router)
    app.include_router(todos.router)

    if FRONTEND_DIR.is_dir():
        # Mounted last so that /api routes take precedence over static files.
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=FRONTEND_DIR, html=True), name="frontend")
    return app


def build() -> FastAPI:
    """Entry point for ``uvicorn --factory app.main:build``: settings from the environment.

    A factory instead of a module-level ``app`` means importing this module
    never needs ``APP_SECRET``, which keeps imports in tests side-effect free.
    """
    return create_app()
```

    </section>
  </main>

  <footer class="footer muted">Taskboard</footer>

  <script type="module">
    import { apiFetch, ApiError, isSignedIn } from "./js/api.js";
    import { el, showMessage } from "./js/ui.js";

    // Navigation depends on whether a token is stored. The server may still
    // reject it later; apiFetch() forgets a rejected token.
    const nav = document.getElementById("nav");
    if (isSignedIn()) {
      nav.append(
        el("a", { href: "todos.html" }, "My todos"),
        el("a", { href: "login.html" }, "Account"),
      );
    } else {
      nav.append(el("a", { href: "login.html" }, "Sign in"));
    }

    // Show that the backend is reachable; a failure here usually means the
    // server is not running or the database cannot be opened.
    try {
      const health = await apiFetch("/api/health");
      document.getElementById("health").textContent =
        `Service is up (version ${health.version}).`;
    } catch (error) {
      const text = error instanceof ApiError ? error.message : "The service cannot be reached.";
      document.getElementById("health").textContent = "";
      showMessage(text, "error");
    }
  </script>
</body>
</html>

// Sign-in and registration.
//
// Both forms call the auth endpoints through apiFetch(). A successful sign-in
// stores the token with saveToken() and sends the user to the todo page; a

// The todo page.
//
// Redirects to the sign-in page when no token is stored, shows the signed-in
// user's name, and lists their todos with paging and a filter. Every change
// goes through apiFetch(); errors are shown with showMessage().

import { apiFetch, ApiError, clearToken, isSignedIn } from "./api.js";
import { clear, el, formValues, showMessage, whileBusy } from "./ui.js";

const PAGE_SIZE = 20;

if (!isSignedIn()) {
  window.location.href = "login.html";
}

const state = {
  offset: 0,
  done: "", // "", "true" or "false"
  total: 0,
  items: [],
};

const listEl = document.getElementById("list");
const emptyEl = document.getElementById("empty");
const countEl = document.getElementById("count");
const rangeEl = document.getElementById("range");
const prevBtn = document.getElementById("prev");
const nextBtn = document.getElementById("next");
const filterEl = document.getElementById("filter");
const addForm = document.getElementById("add-form");
const whoEl = document.getElementById("who");
const signoutBtn = document.getElementById("signout");

/** Show an ApiError, including validation details when present. */
function reportError(error) {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    if (error.code === "invalid_token") {
      window.location.href = "login.html";
      return;
    }
    const details = error.details?.length
      ? " " + error.details.map((d) => `${d.field}: ${d.problem}`).join(" ")
      : "";
    showMessage(error.message + details, "error");
  } else {
    showMessage("Something went wrong. Please try again.", "error");
  }
}

/** Load the current page of todos and render it. */
async function loadTodos() {
  const query = { limit: PAGE_SIZE, offset: state.offset };
  if (state.done !== "") query.done = state.done;
  try {
    const page = await apiFetch("/api/todos", { query });
    state.items = page.items;
    state.total = page.total;
    render();
  } catch (error) {
    reportError(error);
  }
}

/** Render the list, the counter and the pager from the current state. */
function render() {
  clear(listEl);
  for (const todo of state.items) {
    listEl.append(renderItem(todo));
  }
  emptyEl.hidden = state.items.length > 0;

  const first = state.total === 0 ? 0 : state.offset + 1;
  const last = state.offset + state.items.length;
  countEl.textContent = `${state.total} ${state.total === 1 ? "todo" : "todos"}`;
  rangeEl.textContent = state.total === 0 ? "" : `${first}-${last} of ${state.total}`;
  prevBtn.disabled = state.offset === 0;
  nextBtn.disabled = state.offset + state.items.length >= state.total;
}

/** One list item: checkbox, title, rename and delete controls. */
function renderItem(todo) {
  const checkbox = el("input", {
    type: "checkbox",
    checked: todo.done,
    "aria-label": "Done",
    onchange: () => toggleDone(todo, checkbox.checked),
  });

  const title = el("span", { class: "title grow" }, todo.title);

  const renameBtn = el(
    "button",
    { type: "button", class: "secondary", onclick: () => rename(todo) },
    "Rename",
  );
  const deleteBtn = el(
    "button",
    { type: "button", class: "danger", onclick: () => remove(todo) },
    "Delete",
  );

  return el(
    "li",
    { class: todo.done ? "list-item done" : "list-item", dataset: { id: todo.id } },
    checkbox,
    title,
    renameBtn,
    deleteBtn,
  );
}

async function toggleDone(todo, done) {
  try {
    await apiFetch(`/api/todos/${todo.id}`, { method: "PATCH", body: { done } });
    await loadTodos();
  } catch (error) {
    reportError(error);
    await loadTodos();
  }
}

async function rename(todo) {
  const title = window.prompt("New title", todo.title);
  if (title === null) return;
  const trimmed = title.trim();
  if (!trimmed) {
    showMessage("Title must not be empty.", "error");
    return;
  }
  try {
    await apiFetch(`/api/todos/${todo.id}`, { method: "PATCH", body: { title: trimmed } });
    await loadTodos();
  } catch (error) {
    reportError(error);
  }
}

async function remove(todo) {
  if (!window.confirm(`Delete "${todo.title}"?`)) return;
  try {
    await apiFetch(`/api/todos/${todo.id}`, { method: "DELETE" });
    showMessage("Todo deleted.", "success");
    // Step back a page if the last item of this page was removed.
    if (state.items.length === 1 && state.offset > 0) {
      state.offset = Math.max(0, state.offset - PAGE_SIZE);
    }
    await loadTodos();
  } catch (error) {
    reportError(error);
  }
}

addForm.addEventListener("submit", async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const { title } = formValues(addForm);
  if (!title) {
    showMessage("Title must not be empty.", "error");
    return;
  }
  try {
    await whileBusy(addForm, async () => {
      await apiFetch("/api/todos", { method: "POST", body: { title } });
      addForm.reset();
      state.offset = 0;
      await loadTodos();
    });
  } catch (error) {
    reportError(error);
  }
});

filterEl.addEventListener("change", async () => {
  state.done = filterEl.value;
  state.offset = 0;
  await loadTodos();
});

prevBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  state.offset = Math.max(0, state.offset - PAGE_SIZE);
  await loadTodos();
});

nextBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  state.offset += PAGE_SIZE;
  await loadTodos();
});

signoutBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
  clearToken();
  window.location.href = "login.html";
});

// Show the signed-in user's name, then load the first page.
try {
  const me = await apiFetch("/api/auth/me");
  whoEl.textContent = me.username;
} catch (error) {
  reportError(error);
}
await loadTodos();
